findings.note: The commit counter advances only after _atomic_write_bytes returns, but that helper performs os.replace before its parent-directory fsync. If the fsync fails, the target is already live yet is excluded from transaction.committed; rollback can therefore report completion and discard the journal while leaving that POST artifact published, violating the all-or-nothing and AC-039 rollback contract.

Recovery accepts any attacker-controlled journal whose target set matches the Full or Lite bundle and trusts its claimed PRE/POST hashes. A fabricated full-shaped journal can mark an existing artifact's current hash as POST with PRE=ABSENT and a sibling as PRE, causing MIX recovery to unlink the legitimate artifact. The bundle-shape check therefore does not close the destructive-journal threat that this unprotected staging area explicitly treats as attacker-reachable.

Restoring an ABSENT PRE state unlinks the live target without fsyncing its parent directory, after which batch cleanup removes the journal without a durability barrier preserving that ordering. A power loss can persist the journal deletion while losing the target deletion, leaving a POST artifact with no recovery journal and breaking crash-safe convergence.
